draft.title: Impacts of tourism
card: Tourism can bring benefits to a place. It creates jobs in hotels, tours and restaurants, and visitors spend money in the local economy.
Crowding
Too many visitors can fill roads, beaches and paths. Local people may find it hard to use their own town.
Environment
Visitors can trample plants, leave rubbish and disturb wildlife. Building hotels can also clear natural areas.
Culture
Local customs, crafts and ceremonies can change when they are shaped to suit visitors, or when sacred places are treated as attractions.
draft.remember: Tourism can bring jobs and money, but it can also bring crowds, damage and cultural change.

a.q: Walkers on a coastal track in Tasmania keep leaving the path, and the dune plants are dying. Which impact is this?
opts: Damage to the environment
Crowding of local roads
Change to local culture
New jobs for local people
a.why: Plants dying from trampling is harm to the natural environment. Crowding is about too many people in a space, which can happen too, but here the problem is the damage to plants.
a.clue: What is happening to the plants?

b.q: A fishing village in Queensland gains many café jobs as tourists arrive, but locals say they can no longer park near the beach. What does this show?
opts: Tourism can bring benefits and crowding together
Tourism only brings benefits to a small place
Tourism always harms the culture of a village
Tourism causes damage to the environment only
b.why: The new jobs are a benefit, and the lack of parking is crowding, so both appear in one place. The card says tourism can cause problems, not that it only helps or always harms.
b.clue: Sort the jobs and the parking into helps and problems.

b.best: Tourism can bring benefits and crowding together

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is the only one with the qualifier 'can', which matches the card's wording. Every distractor uses 'only' or 'always', so a student who spots the absolute words can pick the answer without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Sort the jobs and the parking into helps and problems' points almost directly at the 'benefits and crowding' option, which adds to the giveaway.
